mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average indicates monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines relative to 12-month moving average, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) >0.5% from prior month indicate aggregate demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and generating negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline >0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when HOUST and INDPRO decline >0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime (INDPRO growth < 0.5% for 3 months), a decline in industrial production below its 6-month average triggers negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced manufacturing output and profit margins.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when INDPRO declines below 6-month average in supply-constrained regime, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential mortgage applications (RSAFS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates housing market expansion, boosting consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when RSAFS rises relative to 12-month moving average, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 250.0 and remains above this level for three consecutive months, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers monetary tightening, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns through higher discount rates.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250.0 for three consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in employment (PAYEMS) >0.3% coupled with a rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) >0.3pp from prior month indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines >0.3% and UNRATE rises >0.3pp from prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when PAYEMS declines >0.3% and UNRATE rises >0.3pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a sustained CPIAUCSL increase above 250.0 triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced real money supply and higher equity discount rates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
